label: 🗼 Galileo's Tower
blurb: Drop a ball straight down from 55 m and watch gravity alone pull it to the ground in ~3 s — no horizontal motion, pure free fall.
callout: Galileo's claim: heavy and light objects fall together. Try it on the Moon (g=1.62).

label: 🎯 Max-range cannon
blurb: Classic 45° artillery shot from ground level — the angle that wrings the most horizontal distance out of a given speed.
callout: From level ground, 45° wins because sin(2θ) peaks there.

label: 🔴 Field goal on Mars
blurb: Same kick, weaker gravity. Watch the ball float much higher and travel three times farther than on Earth.
callout: Lower g stretches time-of-flight; range scales as v₀²/g.

label: 🏔️ Snow on Steel
blurb: Place a heavy steel crate on an oiled steel ramp. Tip the slope past the critical angle and friction snaps — the block slides.
callout: Critical angle: tan(θ_c) = μ_s. Try changing material to see μ_s in action.

label: 🛞 Rubber bites the road
blurb: Dry rubber on concrete clings to a steep ramp without sliding — that's why your tires hold the road on a hill.
callout: High μ_s lets the block stay static at angles a slippery surface couldn't survive.

label: 🎢 Reaches every hill
blurb: A tall first hill banks enough energy to crest every following hill, even with friction nibbling at each segment.
callout: PE→KE→PE handoff; friction slowly drains the total.

label: 🛑 Hill too tall
blurb: A second hill that's taller than the first leaves the cart stranded — gravity gives back exactly what it took, friction makes it worse.
callout: Once total energy < m·g·h_target, the cart cannot climb the hill.

label: 🪀 Newton's Cradle
blurb: Two equal-mass balls in a perfectly elastic head-on collision swap velocities — the swung ball stops, the still ball flies off.
callout: Elastic + equal masses ⇒ perfect velocity swap.

label: 💥 Sticky crash
blurb: Two cars lock bumpers in a perfectly plastic collision. Momentum is preserved, but a huge chunk of KE vanishes into crumpled metal.
callout: Plastic collisions trade KE for deformation — exactly what crumple zones are designed to do.

label: 🎵 Tuning fork (440 Hz)
blurb: A stiff spring on a light mass vibrates fast enough to land near a musical 'A' (~440 Hz when modeled as SHM).
callout: f = 1/(2π)·√(k/m). Higher k or lower m → higher pitch.

label: 🌀 Slow oscillator
blurb: A heavy block on a soft spring takes nearly 2 seconds per swing — visible enough to count beats by hand.
callout: Period grows with √m and shrinks with √k.

label: 💡 Just below threshold
blurb: Aim red light at cesium and crank the intensity to 100%. No matter how bright, frequency is too low — no electrons eject.
callout: Disproves the wave model — intensity doesn't help below f₀ = φ/h.

label: 💜 UV pops electrons
blurb: Switch to a UV lamp on zinc. Each photon now packs more than the work function — electrons fly out with measurable kinetic energy.
callout: KE_max = h·f − φ. Brighter light = more electrons, not faster ones.

label: 🌊 Electron diffraction
blurb: An electron at 1% of light speed has a wavelength comparable to atomic spacing — exactly what makes electron microscopes possible.
callout: λ ≈ 0.24 nm at v = 1% c. Crystals diffract this wavelength.

label: ⚾ Baseball matter wave
blurb: A 145 g baseball at 40 m/s has a wavelength smaller than a proton. That's why we never see baseballs diffract.
callout: λ ≈ 10⁻³⁴ m for everyday objects — wave behavior is completely hidden.
